Team — forwarding PulseHealth's deletion request (attached). They want all production records + backups/snapshots cleared by 2025-07-06 and an auditable proof.

Constraints/context:
- Weekly backup sweep runs every Sunday 02:00 UTC; last full snapshot that may include PH-ICU-2024 is snap-2025-06-22 (retained for 45 days by current policy).
- Some diagnostic logs and KV-cache traces are stored in cold archive for 90 days; forensic team may request a short hold for incident follow-up.
- We have existing DPA language that allows for reasonable forensic holds where required by law/incident.

Options I see (please advise quickly):
A) Comply fully and schedule an immediate expedited purge of all production + snapshots containing identifiers, plus issuance of deletion receipts. Risk: loses ability to investigate any open incidents; may require us to short-circuit backup retention pipeline (coordination w/infra).
B) Propose a limited escrow/rollback pathway: mark affected snapshots as \"quarantined for deletion\" and move copies to an encrypted, access-restricted escrow bucket for 14 days. During that window PulseHealth can request proof; after 14 days we purge escrow and issue receipts. This gives a narrow forensic runway while still meeting an accelerated timeline.
C) Request a 7-day extension to the requested deadline to complete a clean purge across all subprocessor snapshots and produce certified proofs.

I've attached a quick runbook draft (proposed_runbook_escrow_v1.pdf) that outlines the escrow flow, audit logging, and a restore token approach (snapshot-id + HMAC) for secure rollback if PulseHealth discovers something that requires investigation.

Action items: Kimberly — can infra execute a quarantined escrow move and produce tamper-evident deletion receipts within a 14-day window? Laura — legal/ops: would PulseHealth accept a 14-day escrow compromise or insist on absolute deletion by 07/06? Karthik — any subprocessor (S3/GCS backup tenants) implications?

I'll draft a reply to Miguel once I have your quick takes.

Thanks,

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Date: Sun, 29 Jun 2025 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data deletion request for patient subset (DPA Article 17)

Nikhil — quick notes from infra/security after a sync with the ops on-call:

1) Feasibility: We can implement the quarantined escrow move (Option B) as a fast path. Concretely: copy affected snapshots to an encrypted HSM-backed escrow bucket tagged PH-ICU-2024-QUARANTINE, revoke access from operator roles, and apply immutability policy for 14 days (cannot be altered without multi-sig). After 14 days a scheduled purge job will permanently delete the escrow copies and emit a signed deletion manifest (SHA256 + timestamp + operator sig).

2) Evidence: We can produce a tamper-evident deletion receipt bundle containing: list of object keys deleted, SHA256 of deleted object manifests, job-run logs, and a signed statement from infra lead. This meets our internal audit standard and should satisfy most third-party audits.

3) Subprocessor note: Some existing backups are managed by a third-party archiving subprocessor (ArchivaCloud). They have a 72-hour SLA for deletion once we submit a purge request and an API to request signed deletion receipts. We need to submit the deletion job and capture their receipts to include in the final bundle.

4) Risk: If PulseHealth disputes deletion within the 14-day window and requests a full restore, we can restore from the escrow copies but only if the escrow policy permits a restore — that needs PulseHealth sign-off in writing (we should capture that as an amendment to the DPA for the PH-ICU-2024 cohort).

Recommendation: Propose Option B (14-day escrow) to PulseHealth and request their written consent for the restore-policy (even if they never use it). This minimizes legal/regulatory risk while enabling an auditable purging workflow.

I'll attach the infra checklist I used to validate steps in the repo.

-Kim
Director, Platform Security | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Hi Miguel — thanks for the prompt. Internal team has reviewed and we propose the following path to balance PulseHealth's deletion request with a minimal forensic runway:

Proposal (summary):
- Action window: begin quarantined escrow move immediately upon your sign-off; final purge scheduled 14 days after escrow creation (target final purge: 2025-07-14).
- Escrow mechanics: copy affected snapshots to an encrypted, HSM-backed escrow bucket (PH-ICU-2024-QUARANTINE), revoke operator access, and apply an immutability policy for 14 days.
- Proofs: upon purge we'll provide a signed deletion manifest (SHA256 hashes, object keys), infra job logs, and third-party subprocessor receipts from ArchivaCloud where applicable.
- Restore: Redwood can restore from escrow only with written, time-bound written request from PulseHealth; please indicate whether you want a restore option in the amendment below.

Attached: proposed_runbook_escrow_v1.pdf (technical runbook) and a one-line amendment template to the DPA that records PulseHealth's acceptance of the 14-day escrow window and the restore-policy checkbox.

Next steps:
1) If PulseHealth accepts Option B, please sign the amendment (DocuSign link below) and reply with a one-line confirmation.
2) Once we receive your sign-off we will: (a) submit deletion/purge jobs to ArchivaCloud and our storage teams, (b) snapshot escrow and apply immutability, and (c) send an initial escrow manifest proving movement of objects.
